clue.text: Ben Hur was one causing a riot amidst applause

indicators.note: amidst means the phrase a riot sits in the middle of the word for applause

parts.note: a cheer is a shout of applause
taken as written

explanation.surface: A film hero sparks wild disorder while the crowd claps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amidst' puts the phrase 'a riot' as it stands inside the word for applause; 'causing' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Judah Ben-Hur races a chariot in the famous arena scene, so he is a driver of one.

clue.text: Toast counted among one's blessings

definitions.meaning: a toast drunk to someone's wellbeing, as in 'your good ...!'
good physical condition is one of the things people are told to be thankful for

explanation.definitionFit: Glasses are raised to someone's wellbeing, and sound bodily condition is a classic blessing to count.

clue.text: The balance lacks a memorandum

indicators.note: lacks means the following letter is missing from the word for the balance

parts.note: the balance is what is left over, the remainder

explanation.surface: An accountant notes the books are short of a written memo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacks' says a letter goes missing from the word for the balance; the remaining word is a note to jog the memory.
explanation.definitionFit: A memorandum is a note written to prompt recall of something.

clue.text: Path of the swallow ?

parts.note: the swallow is not the bird but the act of swallowing, whose route down from the throat is the gullet

explanation.walkthrough: A swallow's migration route is the false trail: the clue means what you swallow travels through.
explanation.definitionFit: The gullet is the tube food travels down after being swallowed.

clue.text: Going in without work ? So much useless energy

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for going in wraps round the work

parts.note: an entry is the act of going in
OP, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Barging in without doing any job wastes a lot of effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking: the word for going in wraps round the work, an opus.
explanation.definitionFit: In thermodynamics this measures the energy in a system no longer available to do work.

clue.text: It's about the morning paper supply

parts.note: RE means about or concerning
a.m. is the morning

explanation.surface: Something relating to the daily newspaper delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: A quantity of 500 sheets is the standard unit in which writing paper is supplied.

clue.text: Whisky — such a comfort!

parts.note: whisky is jocularly called 'the ...', and 'such a comfort' points to the phrase for material bodily pleasures

explanation.walkthrough: Two ideas meet: 'the creature' is old slang for whisky, and creature comforts are physical luxuries.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish slang calls whiskey 'the crathur', and creature comforts are the small pleasures of life.

clue.text: In agitated style of snooker-player using only a cue?

definitions.text: of snooker-player using only a cue?
definitions.meaning: a snooker player refusing the rest, the cue support, plays without it

explanation.walkthrough: In snooker the rest is a cue-shaped stand to prop the cue on for distant shots; a player using only a cue plays without it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidgeting without pause, and also, split differently, playing without the rest used for long snooker shots.

clue.text: For example The Army Technicians — back issue

indicators.note: back means the whole run of letters built so far is read backwards

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, the British Army's technical corps

explanation.surface: Army engineers return to an old military matter, as an instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the two pieces round as one string. 'issue' is the verb, to come out, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue is to come forth or appear, as a stream issues from a spring.

clue.text: Monkey a doctor found in a swirling stream

indicators.note: found in means the doctor sits inside the other letters
swirling water churns about, so the letters of stream are mixed

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A primate is discovered by a physician in an eddying river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swirling' gives MARSET, the anagram of the river word, and 'found in' sets the doctor inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This small South American primate is a kind of monkey with a long tail.

clue.text: Like a cow or a little pig, including a talking bird

indicators.note: including means the little pig surrounds the bird

parts.note: a runt is the smallest pig of a litter
the mina (myna) is a mimicking bird that can talk

explanation.surface: Farmyard comparison between a cow and a piglet, with a chatty bird thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: The mina, also spelt myna, is an Asian starling that mimics speech; a runt is the weakling of a litter.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle chew the cud, and an animal that does so belongs to this group.

clue.text: African lake country

definitions.meaning: a large shallow lake in north-central Africa
the landlocked state named after that lake

explanation.definitionFit: The same name belongs to a large lake and to the republic around it in central Africa.

clue.text: Gardener Brown's performance potential indicator

definitions.meaning: Lancelot Brown, the 18th-century English landscape gardener, had a famous nickname
a measure of what someone or something is able to do

explanation.walkthrough: 'Capability' Brown designed many great English country-house parks.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancelot Brown said estates had 'capabilities', giving him his nickname; the word also means ability or capacity.

clue.text: The odd North-type house constructed on the square? On the contrary

definitions.text: constructed on the square? On the contrary

indicators.note: odd means strange, so the letters of these words come out in an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A quirky northern-style home built on a town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constructed' looks like the anagram signal, but it belongs to the definition: the square is not built on this, rather the square is built on it, recalling Pythagoras's theorem.
explanation.definitionFit: Pythagoras's theorem concerns the square drawn on the longest side of a right-angled triangle.

clue.text: How a slim lisping lass might describe putting on weight ?

definitions.text: How a slim lisping lass might describe putting on weight ?

parts.words: How a slim lisping lass might describe putting on weight
parts.note: a slim girl would call gaining weight disgusting, and a lisp turns her S into TH

explanation.walkthrough: A lisp turns S into TH, so 'sickening', the slim lass's view of gaining weight, comes out as a word meaning getting fatter.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting fatter is getting thicker, while a lisper saying 'sickening' sounds the same.

clue.text: When to buy specs, or a coronet?

definitions.meaning: the time of life when you start squinting at things
a small crown worn by nobles, standing for noble rank

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is the age for peering; as one it means the rank of the nobility, symbolised by coronets.

clue.text: Extend a Procrustean welcome to a little chap

definitions.text: a Procrustean welcome to a little chap
definitions.meaning: Procrustes, in Greek myth, stretched guests too short for his bed

explanation.walkthrough: Procrustes was the Greek robber who racked short guests and cut down tall ones to fit his bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend is to stretch longer, which is what Procrustes did to his shorter visitors.

clue.text: They nip in on both sides

definitions.text: They nip in on both sides

parts.words: They nip in on both sides
parts.note: a gripping tool whose two jaws close from either side

explanation.definitionFit: The tool grips by closing two jaws together, pinching from left and right.

clue.text: Lauderdale has a vehicle to go abroad

parts.note: a cab is a vehicle
aller is French for to go

explanation.surface: A Scottish earl takes a carriage for a trip overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles II's ministers Clifford, Arlington, Buckingham, Ashley and Lauderdale gave the word CABAL; Lauderdale was one member. 'abroad' says the word is foreign.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duke of Lauderdale was one of the five ministers forming Charles II's cabal, so a plotter of that group.

clue.text: A go-ahead Christian

parts.note: Christian is the hero of Bunyan's allegory of progress, and go-ahead hints at progress

explanation.walkthrough: 'go-ahead' points to progress, as in The Pilgrim's Progress, whose hero is called Christian.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian is the traveller in Bunyan's The Pilgrim's Progress, a man on a devout journey.

clue.text: Transport for sabbath journeying ?

parts.note: a sabbath here is a witches' midnight gathering, and witches traditionally fly to it

explanation.walkthrough: A sabbath is also a witches' midnight meeting, not just the day of rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Witches fly to their gatherings on a broom handle.

clue.text: We hear the lad's employed as harbour-marker

indicators.note: we hear means the word is identified by its sound

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A youngster has a job in the port as a marker.
explanation.definitionFit: A floating marker anchored to show channels or hazards in a harbour.

clue.text: Nothing left, nothing, of an Iberian city

parts.note: O is the round figure nought
port is the left side of a ship
O again for zero

explanation.surface: Nothing remains of a Spanish or Portuguese town.
explanation.walkthrough: Oporto is the English name for Porto, Portugal's second city.
explanation.definitionFit: Porto, known in English as Oporto, is a city in Portugal on the Iberian peninsula.

clue.text: It takes up time for motorists

definitions.text: It takes up time for motorists

parts.words: It takes up time for motorists
parts.note: the phrase for when drivers must switch on lamps puts 'up time' straight after this word

explanation.walkthrough: 'takes up time' means this word is followed by 'up time': lighting-up time, when drivers must turn on lamps.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighting-up time is the hour after which vehicle lamps must be on.

clue.text: First of the month, upset caused on such roads

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective describing roads, as in roads that are frozen

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, the first

indicators.note: upset in a down entry means the month's letters are turned upside down

parts.note: Dec is short for December

explanation.surface: January's first day brings accidents on frozen roads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the month abbreviation upside down (in a down entry) to CED after the numeral one. 'caused on' only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Roads covered with a frozen glaze are described this way.

clue.text: Rare lily found broken in the chaff

indicators.note: broken means the letters are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An unusual flower is discovered crushed among threshing husks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chaff' is the noun for teasing banter, not grain husks.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaff means good-humoured teasing, banter.

clue.text: Small amount for Pussyfoot, passing round hat

indicators.note: passing round means the hat wraps around the other letters

parts.note: a tile is old slang for a hat
Pussyfoot was the nickname of William E. Johnson, a US prohibitionist, so stands for a teetotaller, TT

explanation.surface: A tiny sum is collected for a cat by passing a hat around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pussyfoot' Johnson campaigned for US Prohibition, so the name stands for a teetotaller; 'passing round' has the old slang word for a hat wrap round that abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A tittle is a tiny stroke or jot, hence a very small quantity.

clue.text: Modern go-go variety of underworld VIP

indicators.note: variety of means a different version, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gangland boss runs a trendy go-go dancing club.
explanation.walkthrough: VIP points to a mythical underworld power, not a gangster.
explanation.definitionFit: In medieval and Renaissance legend this is a dreaded deity or demon of the underworld.
